To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the die attach material has the most significant influence on the RthJC of power packages with bottom exposed paddle, the die size is the most significant influence parameter for packages with small die size and the mold compound affects the package that does not have bottom exposed paddle.
the thermal resistance of a power MOSFET package is affected by the package type, die attach material, package size, and interconnection.

the thermal resistance of power devices can be reduced by: 1) using die attach material with higher thermal conductivity; 2) using packages with bottom exposed paddle; and 3) using copper plate as the interconnection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the RthJC of power packages, which has not been studied in detail in the literature.
the thermal performance of power packages with different types and die size, material, and interconnection.
the effects of different package types, sizes, die attach and mold compounds, and interconnections on RthJC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the die size and the die attach material have the most influence on RthIC of the packages studied in this paper.
the RthJC of power device packages can be significantly reduced with proper material selection, interconnection design and package design.

for packages with bottom-exposed die paddle, the die attach material and die size have the most significant influence on RthJc, while for packages without bottom-exposed die paddles, the mold compound and the interconnection are the main factors affecting the RthJc.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the package type, die attach material, die size and interconnection have significant influences on the junction-to- case thermal resistance.
RthJC is strongly affected by the package type, die attach material, die size and interconnection.
the thermal resistance of power packages is highly dependent on the package type, die sizes and material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the package thermal design is not only a function of package type, but also a function of die size, material selection and interconnection.
the thermal performance of the power packages is not only affected by the die size but also the die attach material and interconnection.
RthJC is not only dependent on package type but also die size, material, and interconnection.
